To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the critical success factors of ERP implementation are: business process performance, process orientation, business strategy alignment, organisational change, project management, user involvement, training, and measurement.
the ERP system is a tool for managing and controlling the enterprise's business processes.
the ERP system is a tool that can support business process performance measures in order to achieve business objectives and to improve business competitiveness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a taxonomy of critical factors that influence the ERP success.
the critical success factors of the ERP systems and the way these factors affect the performance of business processes and the organisation as a whole.

how ERP implementation is perceived by practitioners in terms of critical success factors, and the taxonomy is intended to help managers and practitioners to understand ERP implementation process and its critical success factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ERP systems, as an integral part of the business, are built based on the principle of business process re-engineering and therefore, they can only be fully utilised and realised when the business processes are measured and managed based on the principles and concepts of business process management.
, ERP systems have to be designed, implemented and managed based on the principles and practices of business process management, in order to deliver the expected benefits.
, ERP implementation success is a function of the alignment of the implementation approach with the business process performance measures, which in turn is a function of a number of critical factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the ERP implementation process, the critical factors are not only related to the technical and organisational issues, but also the alignment of the two.
the taxonomy of critical factors for ERP implementation is an effective way for the organisation to understand and manage the ERP project.
, ERP systems are not just a technology, but rather a business process oriented management approach that is built on the principles of measurement and alignment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ERP benefits cannot be achieved unless the implementation process is aligned with business processes.
ERP implementation is not a one-time event but an on-going process, which requires continuous monitoring and measurement.
ERP systems are not just about technology, but also about business process performance measures and organisational change management.
